# FluxMedia Documentation

> FluxMedia is a unified media upload library for JavaScript and TypeScript. It provides one API for uploading images, videos, and files to Cloudinary, AWS S3 (and S3-compatible storage), Cloudflare R2, Google Cloud Storage, Azure Blob Storage, or the local filesystem. Write your upload logic once, and it works with every provider.

FluxMedia is an open-source library — not a storage service. It wraps existing providers behind the `MediaProvider` interface, published as npm packages under the `@fluxmedia` scope.

- One API on every provider: `upload`, `get`, `delete`, `getUrl`, `getSignedUrl`, `createUploadUrl`, `exists`, `list`/`listAll`, `copy`, `move`, `download`, `updateMetadata`, `uploadMultiple`, `deleteMultiple`, `uploadWithTransaction`
- Secure browser uploads: `createSignedUploadHandler` and `createProxyUploadHandler` from `@fluxmedia/core/server` require authorization, an allowed-type list and a size limit, decide the folder on the server, and detect file types from content
- Private files: public URLs are optional; time-limited signed URLs on every provider (S3/R2 presigned, GCS V4, Azure SAS, Cloudinary private download or token auth, HMAC for local/R2 bindings)
- Accepts `File`, `Buffer`, Node `Readable` and web `ReadableStream`; byte progress; cancel with `AbortSignal`
- Fallback providers, transactional uploads, retry with backoff
- Plugins via lifecycle hooks: `beforeUpload`, `wrapUpload`, `afterUpload`, `onError`, `beforeDelete`, `afterDelete`, `beforeGetUrl`
- Structured errors with the `MediaErrorCode` enum (including `ABORTED`, `NOT_SUPPORTED`, `RATE_LIMITED`)
- React integration: `useMediaUpload`, `useMediaUploadQueue`, `MediaUpload`
- Only top-level primitive metadata is stored with files; keys and folders are sanitized

## Packages

| Package | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| `@fluxmedia/core` | MediaUploader, plugin system, server upload handlers (`@fluxmedia/core/server`), MemoryProvider, signed-URL helpers, structured errors, file type detection, testing utilities (`@fluxmedia/core/testing`) |
| `@fluxmedia/cloudinary` | Cloudinary provider with transformations |
| `@fluxmedia/s3` | AWS S3 and S3-compatible storage (MinIO, Backblaze B2, Wasabi, DigitalOcean Spaces, Supabase Storage) |
| `@fluxmedia/r2` | Cloudflare R2 provider (S3 API) and R2BindingProvider for Workers |
| `@fluxmedia/gcs` | Google Cloud Storage provider |
| `@fluxmedia/azure` | Azure Blob Storage provider |
| `@fluxmedia/local` | Local filesystem provider and file-serving handler |
| `@fluxmedia/react` | React hooks and components |
| `@fluxmedia/plugins` | Official plugins: validation, image optimization, metadata extraction, virus scanning, deduplication, placeholders, analytics, retry |

---

<!-- Source: https://www.fluxmedia.dev/docs/getting-started -->

## Getting Started

Learn how to install and configure FluxMedia in your project.

### Installation

Choose your package manager:

```bash npm2yarn
npm install @fluxmedia/core @fluxmedia/cloudinary
```

#### Available Packages

Install only what you need:

```bash
# Core (required)
pnpm add @fluxmedia/core

# Pick a provider (each needs its SDK as a peer dependency)
pnpm add @fluxmedia/cloudinary cloudinary                                  # Transformations
pnpm add @fluxmedia/s3 @aws-sdk/client-s3 @aws-sdk/lib-storage            # AWS S3 / S3-compatible
pnpm add @fluxmedia/r2 @aws-sdk/client-s3 @aws-sdk/lib-storage            # Cloudflare R2
pnpm add @fluxmedia/gcs @google-cloud/storage                             # Google Cloud Storage
pnpm add @fluxmedia/azure @azure/storage-blob                             # Azure Blob Storage
pnpm add @fluxmedia/local                                                 # Local filesystem

# Signed URLs on S3/R2
pnpm add @aws-sdk/s3-request-presigner

# Optional: Official plugins
pnpm add @fluxmedia/plugins

# Optional: React integration
pnpm add @fluxmedia/react
```

For tests and local development, `MemoryProvider` from `@fluxmedia/core` needs no setup.

## Core (required)
pnpm add @fluxmedia/core

## Pick a provider
pnpm add @fluxmedia/cloudinary  # Full featured with transformations
pnpm add @fluxmedia/s3          # AWS S3
pnpm add @fluxmedia/r2          # Cloudflare R2

## Optional: Official plugins
pnpm add @fluxmedia/plugins

## Optional: React integration
pnpm add @fluxmedia/react
```

## Basic Usage

### Node.js / Server

```typescript
import { MediaUploader } from '@fluxmedia/core';
import { CloudinaryProvider } from '@fluxmedia/cloudinary';

// Create uploader with your provider
const uploader = new MediaUploader(
  new CloudinaryProvider({
    cloudName: process.env.CLOUDINARY_CLOUD_NAME!,
    apiKey: process.env.CLOUDINARY_API_KEY!,
    apiSecret: process.env.CLOUDINARY_API_SECRET!,
  })
);

// Upload a file
const result = await uploader.upload(fileBuffer, {
  folder: 'user-avatars',
  filename: 'avatar-123',
});

console.log(result.url); // https://res.cloudinary.com/...
console.log(result.id); // user-avatars/avatar-123-x1y2z3a4 (random suffix; uniqueFilename: false to keep the exact name)
console.log(result.storageKey); // Provider-specific storage key
console.log(result.format); // jpg
```

Folders and filenames are sanitized, and only top-level string, number and boolean `metadata` values are stored with the file.

### Streaming Uploads

FluxMedia accepts multiple input types — not just `File` and `Buffer`:

```typescript
import { createReadStream } from 'fs';

// Upload from Node.js Readable stream
const stream = createReadStream('/path/to/large-file.mp4');
const result = await uploader.upload(stream, {
  folder: 'videos',
  contentType: 'video/mp4', // streams cannot be sniffed, so set the type
});

// Upload from web ReadableStream
const response = await fetch('https://example.com/image.jpg');
const result = await uploader.upload(response.body!, {
  folder: 'imports',
  contentType: response.headers.get('content-type') ?? 'application/octet-stream',
});
```

A stream can only be read once, so stream uploads are never retried or sent to a fallback provider.

### With React

The browser asks your server for a signed upload target, then uploads straight to storage:

```tsx
import { useMediaUpload } from '@fluxmedia/react';

function UploadButton() {
  const { upload, cancel, uploading, progress, result, error } = useMediaUpload({
    mode: 'signed',
    signUrlEndpoint: '/api/upload/sign',
    accept: ['image/*'],
    maxSize: 10 * 1024 * 1024,
  });

  return (
    <input
      type="file"
      disabled={uploading}
      onChange={(e) => {
        const file = e.target.files?.[0];
        if (file) upload(file);
      }}
    />
  );
}
```

The endpoint is one handler:

```typescript
// app/api/upload/sign/route.ts
import { createSignedUploadHandler } from '@fluxmedia/core/server';

export const POST = createSignedUploadHandler(uploader, {
  authorize: (request) => getSessionUser(request),
  allowedTypes: ['image/jpeg', 'image/png', 'image/webp'],
  maxSize: 10 * 1024 * 1024,
  folder: (user) => `users/${user.id}`,
});
```

See [Secure Uploads](/docs/secure-uploads) for the proxy alternative and the security checklist.

## Using Multiple Providers

FluxMedia lets you use multiple providers in the same application with a consistent API:

```typescript
// Cloudinary for media
const uploader = new MediaUploader(
  new CloudinaryProvider({ ... })
);

// S3 for archives — same interface
import { S3Provider } from '@fluxmedia/s3';

const uploader = new MediaUploader(
  new S3Provider({
    region: 'us-east-1',
    bucket: 'my-bucket',
    accessKeyId: process.env.AWS_ACCESS_KEY!,
    secretAccessKey: process.env.AWS_SECRET_KEY!,
  })
);

// All your upload code stays exactly the same
await uploader.upload(file, { folder: 'uploads' });
```

## Fallback Providers

Configure automatic failover when the primary provider is unavailable:

```typescript
import { MediaUploader, MediaErrorCode } from '@fluxmedia/core';

const uploader = new MediaUploader(
  new CloudinaryProvider({ ... }),  // Primary
  [],                                // No plugins
  {
    fallbackProvider: new S3Provider({ ... }),  // Fallback
    fallbackOnErrors: [
      MediaErrorCode.NETWORK_ERROR,
      MediaErrorCode.RATE_LIMITED,
      MediaErrorCode.PROVIDER_ERROR,
    ],
    onFallback: (error, fromProvider, toProvider) => {
      console.warn(`Using ${toProvider} instead of ${fromProvider}: ${error.message}`);
    },
  }
);

// If Cloudinary fails with a qualifying error, S3 is used automatically
const result = await uploader.upload(file, { folder: 'uploads' });

// Pass the result (not just the ID) so later calls go to the provider that stored it
await uploader.delete(result);
```

## Upload with Abort

Cancel in-flight uploads using `AbortController`:

```typescript
const controller = new AbortController();

// Cancel after 30 seconds
setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), 30000);

const result = await uploader.upload(file, {
  folder: 'uploads',
  signal: controller.signal,
});
```

## Progress Tracking

Track upload progress at two levels:

```typescript
const result = await uploader.upload(file, {
  folder: 'uploads',
  onProgress: (percent) => {
    // Normalized 0-100 percentage
    progressBar.style.width = `${percent}%`;
  },
  onByteProgress: (loaded, total) => {
    // Raw byte counts for precise tracking
    console.log(`${loaded}/${total} bytes`);
  },
});
```

## Feature Detection

Check if a provider supports specific features:

```typescript
if (uploader.supports('transformations.resize')) {
  // Apply resize transformation
  const url = uploader.getUrl(id, { width: 200, height: 200 });
}

if (uploader.supports('capabilities.videoProcessing')) {
  // Provider supports video processing
}
```

## Private Files

Leave the public URL off and hand out short-lived links:

```typescript
const result = await uploader.upload(file);
const url = await uploader.getSignedUrl(result, { expiresIn: 300 });
```

Each provider page explains how to make storage private (for example `publicUrl: false` on S3, or no `publicUrl` on R2).

## Providers

FluxMedia supports multiple cloud storage providers through a unified API.

### Available Providers

| Provider | Package | Transformations | Signed URLs | Signed browser uploads |
|----------|---------|-----------------|-------------|------------------------|
| [Cloudinary](/docs/cloudinary) | `@fluxmedia/cloudinary` | Full | Yes | Yes (format enforced) |
| [AWS S3](/docs/s3) | `@fluxmedia/s3` | No | Yes | Yes (type and size enforced) |
| [Cloudflare R2](/docs/r2) | `@fluxmedia/r2` | No | Yes | Yes (type and size enforced) |
| [Google Cloud Storage](/docs/gcs) | `@fluxmedia/gcs` | No | Yes | Yes (type and max size enforced) |
| [Azure Blob Storage](/docs/azure) | `@fluxmedia/azure` | No | Yes | Yes (not enforced) |
| [Local filesystem](/docs/local) | `@fluxmedia/local` | No | Yes (HMAC) | No |
| In-memory | `@fluxmedia/core` (`MemoryProvider`) | No | Yes (HMAC) | No |

All providers support `list`, `copy`, `move`, `download`, `exists` and `updateMetadata`. Search is Cloudinary-only.

### Choosing a Provider

#### Cloudinary
Best for: **Applications needing image/video transformations**

- Resize, crop, format conversion on-the-fly
- AI-powered tagging and face detection
- Video transcoding and streaming
- Higher cost but more features

#### AWS S3
Best for: **Simple file storage with AWS integration**

- Reliable and widely used; IAM roles and the default credential chain work out of the box
- CloudFront for delivery (`publicUrl`), Lambda@Edge for transformations
- Also covers S3-compatible services: MinIO, Backblaze B2, Wasabi, DigitalOcean Spaces, Supabase Storage

#### Cloudflare R2
Best for: **Cost-effective storage with zero egress fees**

- S3-compatible API, or bucket bindings inside Cloudflare Workers
- No egress fees (great for high-traffic)
- Use with Cloudflare Images for transformations

#### Google Cloud Storage
Best for: **Applications on Google Cloud**

- Application Default Credentials (Workload Identity, Cloud Run service accounts)
- V4 signed URLs with a size cap on browser uploads

#### Azure Blob Storage
Best for: **Applications on Azure**

- Shared key or Microsoft Entra ID (user delegation SAS)
- Block blob streaming for large files

#### Local filesystem
Best for: **Development, tests and single-server self-hosting**

- No account or SDK needed
- Includes a file-serving handler with safe headers and signed-URL checks

### Custom Providers

You can create custom providers by implementing the `MediaProvider` interface:

```typescript
import type { MediaProvider, UploadResult } from '@fluxmedia/core';
import { buildStorageKey, assertSafeKey, detectContentInfo, toPersistedMetadata } from '@fluxmedia/core';

class MyProvider implements MediaProvider {
  name = 'my-provider';

  features = {
    transformations: { resize: false, crop: false, ... },
    capabilities: { signedUploads: true, signedUrls: true, list: true, ... },
    storage: { maxFileSize: 100_000_000, supportedFormats: ['*'] },
  };

  async upload(file, options) {
    const key = buildStorageKey(options ?? {});            // sanitized key
    const info = await detectContentInfo(file, options);    // type from content
    const metadata = toPersistedMetadata(options?.metadata); // primitives only
    // Your upload logic
    return { id: key, storageKey: key, url, ... };
  }

  async delete(id, options?) { assertSafeKey(id, this.name); ... }
  async get(id, options?) { ... }
  getUrl(id, transform?, options?) { ... }
  async uploadMultiple(files, options) { ... }
  async deleteMultiple(ids, options?) { ... }
  get native() { return this.client; }

  // Optional: getSignedUrl, createUploadUrl, exists, list, search,
  // copy, move, download, updateMetadata
}
```

`MediaUploader` throws a `NOT_SUPPORTED` error for optional methods your provider leaves out. Use contract tests to verify your provider implementation:

```typescript
import { createProviderContractTests } from '@fluxmedia/core/testing';

createProviderContractTests('MyProvider', () => new MyProvider({ ... }));
```

This validates required properties, feature matrix structure, all required methods, and URL generation.

---

<!-- Source: https://www.fluxmedia.dev/docs/cloudinary -->

## Cloudinary Provider

Full-featured media management with on-the-fly transformations.

### Installation

```bash
pnpm add @fluxmedia/core @fluxmedia/cloudinary cloudinary
```

### Configuration

```typescript
import { MediaUploader } from '@fluxmedia/core';
import { CloudinaryProvider } from '@fluxmedia/cloudinary';

const uploader = new MediaUploader(
  new CloudinaryProvider({
    cloudName: 'your-cloud-name',
    apiKey: 'your-api-key',
    apiSecret: 'your-api-secret',
    secure: true, // Use HTTPS (default: true)
  })
);
```

#### Configuration Options

| Option               | Type    | Required | Description                                                         |
| -------------------- | ------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `cloudName`          | string  | Yes      | Your Cloudinary cloud name                                          |
| `apiKey`             | string  | Yes      | API key from dashboard                                              |
| `apiSecret`          | string  | Yes      | API secret (keep secure!)                                           |
| `secure`             | boolean | No       | Use HTTPS URLs (default: true)                                      |
| `authTokenKey`       | string  | No       | Token-based auth key: expiring URLs for private assets, with transformations |
| `secureDistribution` | string  | No       | Custom delivery domain (CNAME / private CDN)                        |

Credentials are sent with each request rather than through the global `cloudinary.config()`, so providers for different accounts can run in one process.

### Upload with Transformations

```typescript
const result = await uploader.upload(file, {
  folder: 'avatars',
  tags: ['user', 'profile'],
  transformation: {
    width: 400,
    height: 400,
    fit: 'cover',
    quality: 80,
    format: 'webp',
  },
});
```

### On-the-fly URL Transformations

```typescript
// Get URL with transformations
const thumbnail = uploader.getUrl(result.id, {
  width: 150,
  height: 150,
  fit: 'cover',
  format: 'webp',
});

// Multiple sizes
const sizes = {
  small: uploader.getUrl(id, { width: 100 }),
  medium: uploader.getUrl(id, { width: 400 }),
  large: uploader.getUrl(id, { width: 800 }),
};
```

### Batch Uploads

```typescript
const results = await uploader.uploadMultiple(files, {
  folder: 'batch-upload',
  concurrency: 5,
  onBatchProgress: (completed, total) => {
    console.log(`Uploaded ${completed}/${total} files`);
  }
});
```

### Delete Files

```typescript
// Pass the upload result: the provider knows the resource type (image, video, raw)
await uploader.delete(result);

// With only an ID, give the resource type, or the provider tries image, video and raw in turn
await uploader.delete(videoId, { metadata: { resourceType: 'video' } });

// Delete multiple
await uploader.deleteMultiple(['id1', 'id2', 'id3']);
```

### Private Assets and Signed URLs

```typescript
// Stored as "authenticated": no public URL, readable only through signed URLs
const result = await uploader.upload(file, { public: false });

const url = await uploader.getSignedUrl(result, { expiresIn: 600 });
```

For private assets, signed URLs use Cloudinary's private download API (original file, real expiry), or, with `authTokenKey`, token-authenticated delivery URLs that also support transformations. Public assets are readable by anyone, so `getSignedUrl` returns their normal URL. Pass the `UploadResult` to skip an Admin API lookup.

### Direct Browser Uploads

`createUploadUrl` returns signed form fields for a `POST` to the Cloudinary upload API. The signature fixes the public ID, tags, context, delivery type and allowed formats; it cannot cap the file size, so use an upload preset with limits (or the proxy handler) when size matters. See [Secure Uploads](/docs/secure-uploads).

### Listing and Search

```typescript
const page = await uploader.list({ folder: 'products', limit: 50 });
const results = await uploader.search({ query: 'shoe', tags: ['summer'] });
```

Both use the Search API, which indexes new uploads asynchronously. `copy`, `move` (rename), `download`, `exists` and `updateMetadata` (context) are also supported.

### Supported Features

```typescript
uploader.supports('transformations.resize')   // true
uploader.supports('transformations.crop')     // true
uploader.supports('transformations.format')   // true
uploader.supports('transformations.quality')  // true
uploader.supports('transformations.blur')     // true
uploader.supports('capabilities.aiTagging')   // true
uploader.supports('capabilities.videoProcessing') // true
uploader.supports('capabilities.signedUrls')  // true
uploader.supports('capabilities.search')      // true
```

### Native SDK Access

Access the full Cloudinary SDK for advanced operations. The global config is not set, so pass credentials with each call:

```typescript
const cloudinary = uploader.provider.native; // null until the first request

const credentials = {
  cloud_name: process.env.CLOUDINARY_CLOUD_NAME,
  api_key: process.env.CLOUDINARY_API_KEY,
  api_secret: process.env.CLOUDINARY_API_SECRET,
};

await cloudinary.uploader.explicit('sample', {
  ...credentials,
  type: 'upload',
  eager: [{ effect: 'sepia' }],
});
```

### Environment Variables

```bash
CLOUDINARY_CLOUD_NAME=your-cloud-name
CLOUDINARY_API_KEY=your-api-key
CLOUDINARY_API_SECRET=your-api-secret
```

<!-- Source: https://www.fluxmedia.dev/docs/s3 -->

## AWS S3 Provider

Simple, reliable file storage with the AWS ecosystem.

### Installation

```bash
pnpm add @fluxmedia/core @fluxmedia/s3 @aws-sdk/client-s3 @aws-sdk/lib-storage
```

### Configuration

```typescript
import { MediaUploader } from '@fluxmedia/core';
import { S3Provider } from '@fluxmedia/s3';

const uploader = new MediaUploader(
  new S3Provider({
    region: 'us-east-1',
    bucket: 'my-media-bucket',
    accessKeyId: process.env.AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID!,
    secretAccessKey: process.env.AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY!,
  })
);
```

#### Configuration Options

| Option            | Type                | Required | Description                                                                 |
| ----------------- | ------------------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `region`          | string              | Yes\*    | AWS region (e.g., 'us-east-1')                                              |
| `bucket`          | string              | Yes      | S3 bucket name                                                              |
| `accessKeyId`     | string              | No       | Access key. Without keys, the AWS default credential chain is used (IAM roles, SSO, env vars) |
| `secretAccessKey` | string              | No       | Secret key (required with `accessKeyId`)                                    |
| `sessionToken`    | string              | No       | Temporary (STS) credentials                                                 |
| `credentials`     | object / provider   | No       | Credentials or a credential provider                                        |
| `client`          | S3Client            | No       | Use an existing client                                                      |
| `clientConfig`    | object              | No       | Extra `S3Client` options                                                    |
| `endpoint`        | string              | No       | Custom endpoint (for S3-compatible services)                                |
| `forcePathStyle`  | boolean             | No       | Force path style URLs                                                       |
| `publicUrl`       | string \| false     | No       | CDN base URL (CloudFront), or `false` for a private bucket                  |
| `useAcl`          | boolean             | No       | Apply `public` as an object ACL (ACL-enabled buckets only)                  |
| `appendExtension` | boolean             | No       | Append the detected extension to generated keys                             |
| `multipart`       | object              | No       | `{ partSize, queueSize }` for multipart uploads                             |

\*Not required when you pass `client`.

### Basic Usage

```typescript
const result = await uploader.upload(file, {
  folder: 'uploads',
  filename: 'photo',
});

console.log(result.storageKey); // uploads/photo-x1y2z3a4 (random suffix unless uniqueFilename: false)
console.log(result.url);
// https://my-media-bucket.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/uploads/photo-x1y2z3a4
```

Folders and filenames are sanitized, so a key can never escape the bucket root. Only top-level string, number and boolean `metadata` values are stored (as `x-amz-meta-*` headers).

### Upload with Progress

```typescript
const result = await uploader.upload(file, {
  folder: 'uploads',
  onProgress: (percent) => {
    console.log(`Upload progress: ${percent}%`);
  },
  onByteProgress: (loaded, total) => {
    console.log(`${loaded}/${total} bytes`);
  },
});
```

### Batch Uploads

Upload multiple files with concurrency control:

```typescript
const results = await uploader.uploadMultiple(files, {
  folder: 'batch-uploads',
  concurrency: 5,
  onBatchProgress: (completed, total) => {
    console.log(`Uploaded ${completed}/${total} files`);
  },
});
```

### S3-Compatible Services

Works with MinIO, Backblaze B2, Wasabi, DigitalOcean Spaces, Supabase Storage and other S3-compatible services:

```typescript
// DigitalOcean Spaces
new S3Provider({
  region: 'nyc3',
  bucket: 'my-space',
  accessKeyId: 'your-spaces-key',
  secretAccessKey: 'your-spaces-secret',
  endpoint: 'https://nyc3.digitaloceanspaces.com',
});

// MinIO
new S3Provider({
  region: 'us-east-1',
  bucket: 'my-bucket',
  accessKeyId: 'minio-access-key',
  secretAccessKey: 'minio-secret-key',
  endpoint: 'http://localhost:9000',
  forcePathStyle: true,
});

// Backblaze B2
new S3Provider({
  region: 'us-west-004',
  bucket: 'my-bucket',
  accessKeyId: process.env.B2_KEY_ID,
  secretAccessKey: process.env.B2_APPLICATION_KEY,
  endpoint: 'https://s3.us-west-004.backblazeb2.com',
});

// Supabase Storage (S3 protocol)
new S3Provider({
  region: 'us-east-1',
  bucket: 'media',
  accessKeyId: process.env.SUPABASE_S3_KEY_ID,
  secretAccessKey: process.env.SUPABASE_S3_SECRET,
  endpoint: 'https://<project-ref>.supabase.co/storage/v1/s3',
  forcePathStyle: true,
});
```

### Private Buckets and Signed URLs

```typescript
const uploader = new MediaUploader(
  new S3Provider({ region: 'us-east-1', bucket: 'private-bucket', publicUrl: false })
);

const result = await uploader.upload(file);    // result.publicUrl is undefined
const url = await uploader.getSignedUrl(result, { expiresIn: 300, downloadAs: 'report.pdf' });
```

For direct browser uploads, `createUploadUrl` returns a presigned `PUT` whose content type and exact size are part of the signature, so S3 rejects any other file. Expose it through `createSignedUploadHandler` — see [Secure Uploads](/docs/secure-uploads). Signed URLs need `@aws-sdk/s3-request-presigner`.

### CloudFront

```typescript
new S3Provider({ region: 'us-east-1', bucket: 'media', publicUrl: 'https://d111111abcdef8.cloudfront.net' });
```

### File Operations

```typescript
await uploader.list({ folder: 'invoices', limit: 100 });   // ListObjectsV2, cursor-based
await uploader.copy(result, 'archive/2026/report.pdf');    // CopyObject
await uploader.move(result, 'archive/report.pdf');         // copy + delete
await uploader.updateMetadata(result, { status: 'final' }); // keeps storage class and encryption
const { body } = await uploader.download(result);          // ReadableStream
await uploader.deleteMultiple(['a.png', 'b.png']);         // DeleteObjects, 1000 per request
```

Uploads can be cancelled with `signal`; failed multipart uploads are aborted so no orphaned parts are billed.

### Supported Features

S3 is storage-only (no transformations):

```typescript
uploader.supports('transformations.resize'); // false
uploader.supports('capabilities.signedUploads'); // true
uploader.supports('capabilities.signedUrls'); // true
uploader.supports('capabilities.multipartUpload'); // true
uploader.supports('capabilities.list'); // true
```

### Native SDK Access

Access the underlying AWS S3 client for advanced operations:

```typescript
import type { S3Provider } from '@fluxmedia/s3';

const s3Client = await (uploader.provider as S3Provider).getClient();

const { ListBucketsCommand } = await import('@aws-sdk/client-s3');
const buckets = await s3Client.send(new ListBucketsCommand({}));
```

### Environment Variables

```bash
AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=your-access-key
AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=your-secret-key
AWS_REGION=us-east-1
S3_BUCKET=my-bucket
```

### Adding Transformations

Use CloudFront + Lambda@Edge for image transformations, or consider [Cloudinary](/docs/cloudinary) for built-in support.

---

<!-- Source: https://www.fluxmedia.dev/docs/r2 -->

## Cloudflare R2 Provider

Cost-effective storage with zero egress fees.

### Installation

```bash
pnpm add @fluxmedia/core @fluxmedia/r2 @aws-sdk/client-s3 @aws-sdk/lib-storage
```

R2 uses the S3-compatible API, so it requires `@aws-sdk/client-s3`.

### Configuration

```typescript
import { MediaUploader } from '@fluxmedia/core';
import { R2Provider } from '@fluxmedia/r2';

const uploader = new MediaUploader(
  new R2Provider({
    accountId: 'your-cloudflare-account-id',
    bucket: 'my-bucket',
    accessKeyId: 'your-r2-access-key',
    secretAccessKey: 'your-r2-secret-key',
    publicUrl: 'https://cdn.example.com', // Optional: custom domain
  })
);
```

#### Configuration Options

| Option            | Type     | Required | Description                                               |
| ----------------- | -------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `accountId`       | string   | Yes\*    | Cloudflare account ID                                     |
| `endpoint`        | string   | Yes\*    | R2 endpoint (alternative to accountId)                    |
| `jurisdiction`    | string   | No       | `'eu'` or `'fedramp'` endpoints (with `accountId`)        |
| `bucket`          | string   | Yes      | R2 bucket name                                            |
| `accessKeyId`     | string   | Yes      | R2 API token access key                                   |
| `secretAccessKey` | string   | Yes      | R2 API token secret key                                   |
| `publicUrl`       | string   | No       | Public base URL (omit for a private bucket)               |
| `appendExtension` | boolean  | No       | Append the detected extension to generated keys           |
| `client`          | S3Client | No       | Use an existing client                                    |

\*Either `accountId` or `endpoint` is required.

### Getting R2 Credentials

1. Go to [Cloudflare Dashboard](https://dash.cloudflare.com) → R2
2. Create a bucket
3. Click "Manage R2 API Tokens"
4. Create a token with read/write permissions
5. Copy the Access Key ID and Secret Access Key

### Basic Usage

```typescript
const result = await uploader.upload(file, {
  folder: 'uploads',
});

console.log(result.url);
// https://cdn.example.com/uploads/file.jpg
console.log(result.storageKey); // uploads/file.jpg
```

### Upload with Progress

```typescript
const result = await uploader.upload(file, {
  folder: 'uploads',
  onProgress: (percent) => {
    console.log(`Upload progress: ${percent}%`);
  },
  onByteProgress: (loaded, total) => {
    console.log(`${loaded}/${total} bytes`);
  },
});
```

### Batch Uploads

```typescript
const results = await uploader.uploadMultiple(files, {
  folder: 'batch-uploads',
  concurrency: 5,
  onBatchProgress: (completed, total) => {
    console.log(`Uploaded ${completed}/${total} files`);
  },
});
```

### Why R2?

- **Zero egress fees** - Free outbound data transfer
- **S3-compatible** - Easy migration from S3
- **Global distribution** - Cloudflare's edge network
- **Cost-effective** - Only pay for storage and operations

### Signed URLs and File Operations

`R2Provider` is an `S3Provider` configured for R2, so it supports `getSignedUrl`, `createUploadUrl` (content type and exact size are signed), `list`, `copy`, `move`, `download` and `updateMetadata`. R2 has no object ACLs: `public: true` on a private bucket (or `public: false` on a public one) is rejected rather than ignored. See [Secure Uploads](/docs/secure-uploads) for browser uploads.

### Cloudflare Workers (bucket bindings)

In a Worker, use the R2 binding directly — no AWS SDK and no credentials:

```typescript
import { MediaUploader } from '@fluxmedia/core';
import { R2BindingProvider } from '@fluxmedia/r2';

export default {
  async fetch(request: Request, env: Env) {
    const uploader = new MediaUploader(
      new R2BindingProvider({
        bucket: env.MEDIA,
        // Optional: signed links served by your own Worker route
        signedUrlBase: 'https://media.example.com/files',
        signingSecret: env.MEDIA_SECRET,
      })
    );
    const result = await uploader.upload(request.body!, { contentType: 'image/png' });
    return Response.json(result);
  },
};
```

Bindings cannot presign URLs, so `getSignedUrl()` returns an HMAC-signed link to your route; check it there with `verifySignedUrl()` from `@fluxmedia/core`. Streams must have a known length.

### Supported Features

R2 is storage-only:

```typescript
uploader.supports('transformations.resize'); // false
uploader.supports('capabilities.signedUploads'); // true
uploader.supports('capabilities.signedUrls'); // true
uploader.supports('capabilities.multipartUpload'); // true
```

### Native SDK Access

Access the underlying S3-compatible client:

```typescript
import type { R2Provider } from '@fluxmedia/r2';

const client = await (uploader.provider as R2Provider).getClient();

const { ListObjectsV2Command } = await import('@aws-sdk/client-s3');
const objects = await client.send(new ListObjectsV2Command({ Bucket: 'my-bucket' }));
```

### Adding Transformations

Use [Cloudflare Images](https://developers.cloudflare.com/images/) for image transformations, or consider [Cloudinary](/docs/cloudinary) for built-in support.

### Environment Variables

```bash
CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID=your-account-id
R2_BUCKET=my-bucket
R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID=your-access-key
R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=your-secret-key
# Optional: omit for a private bucket
R2_PUBLIC_URL=https://cdn.example.com
```

---

<!-- Source: https://www.fluxmedia.dev/docs/gcs -->

## Google Cloud Storage Provider

Google Cloud Storage provider for [FluxMedia](https://www.fluxmedia.dev).

```bash
pnpm add @fluxmedia/core @fluxmedia/gcs @google-cloud/storage
```

```typescript
import { MediaUploader } from '@fluxmedia/core';
import { GCSProvider } from '@fluxmedia/gcs';

const uploader = new MediaUploader(
  new GCSProvider({
    bucket: 'my-bucket',
    // Without credentials, Application Default Credentials are used
    // (Workload Identity, Cloud Run / GCE service accounts, gcloud auth).
    publicUrl: false, // private bucket: serve with getSignedUrl()
  })
);

const result = await uploader.upload(file, { folder: 'docs' });
const url = await uploader.getSignedUrl(result, { expiresIn: 600 });
```

- Streams, and files above 8 MB, use resumable uploads, with byte progress and cancel (`signal`).
- `getSignedUrl()` and `createUploadUrl()` use V4 signing (max 7 days). Upload URLs sign the content type and, with `size`, cap the upload with `x-goog-content-length-range`.
- Supports `list` (page tokens), `copy`, `move`, `download`, `updateMetadata` and `exists`.

**Signing credentials.** Signed URLs need a credential that can sign: a service account key, or — on Cloud Run, GKE or GCE with Application Default Credentials — the service account needs the `iam.serviceAccounts.signBlob` permission (role "Service Account Token Creator" on itself), because signing then goes through the IAM API.

### Configuration

| Option               | Type            | Description                                                         |
| -------------------- | --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `bucket`             | string          | Bucket name (required)                                              |
| `projectId`          | string          | Project ID                                                          |
| `keyFilename`        | string          | Service account key file                                            |
| `credentials`        | object          | Service account credentials                                         |
| `storage`            | Storage         | Existing client                                                     |
| `publicUrl`          | string \| false | CDN/base URL, `false` for private, unset for `storage.googleapis.com` |
| `useAcl`             | boolean         | Apply `public` as an object ACL (fine-grained buckets only)         |
| `appendExtension`    | boolean         | Append the detected extension to keys                               |
| `resumableThreshold` | number          | Size above which uploads are resumable (default 8 MB)               |

Browser uploads need a bucket CORS rule allowing `PUT` with the `Content-Type` and `x-goog-*` headers.

---

<!-- Source: https://www.fluxmedia.dev/docs/azure -->

## Azure Blob Storage Provider

Azure Blob Storage provider for [FluxMedia](https://www.fluxmedia.dev).

```bash
pnpm add @fluxmedia/core @fluxmedia/azure @azure/storage-blob
```

```typescript
import { MediaUploader } from '@fluxmedia/core';
import { AzureBlobProvider } from '@fluxmedia/azure';

// Shared key
const uploader = new MediaUploader(
  new AzureBlobProvider({
    container: 'media',
    connectionString: process.env.AZURE_STORAGE_CONNECTION_STRING,
    publicUrl: false, // private container: serve with getSignedUrl()
  })
);

// Or Microsoft Entra ID (signed URLs then use a user delegation SAS)
import { DefaultAzureCredential } from '@azure/identity';
new AzureBlobProvider({
  container: 'media',
  accountName: 'myaccount',
  credential: new DefaultAzureCredential(),
});
```

- Buffers upload with `uploadData`; streams and Files stream in 8 MB blocks, with byte progress and cancel (`signal`).
- `getSignedUrl()` returns a read SAS (account key or user delegation key, max 7 days).
- `createUploadUrl()` returns a create/write SAS for a `PUT` with `x-ms-blob-type: BlockBlob`. Azure SAS cannot restrict content type or size, so check uploads afterwards or use the proxy handler when that matters.
- Metadata keys are converted to valid identifiers (`user-id` becomes `user_id`).
- Supports `list` (continuation tokens), `copy`, `move`, `download`, `updateMetadata` and `exists`.

### Configuration

| Option             | Type              | Description                                               |
| ------------------ | ----------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `container`        | string            | Container name (required)                                 |
| `connectionString` | string            | Storage account connection string                         |
| `accountName`      | string            | Account name, with `accountKey` or `credential`           |
| `accountKey`       | string            | Shared key                                                |
| `credential`       | TokenCredential   | Entra ID credential                                       |
| `serviceClient`    | BlobServiceClient | Existing client                                           |
| `publicUrl`        | string \| false   | CDN/base URL, `false` for private, unset for the blob URL |
| `appendExtension`  | boolean           | Append the detected extension to keys                     |
| `blockSize`        | number            | Block size for streamed uploads (default 8 MB)            |
| `concurrency`      | number            | Parallel block uploads (default 4)                        |

<!-- Source: https://www.fluxmedia.dev/docs/local -->

## Local Filesystem Provider

Local filesystem provider for [FluxMedia](https://www.fluxmedia.dev). Use it for development, tests, self-hosting and single-server deployments.

```bash
pnpm add @fluxmedia/core @fluxmedia/local
```

```typescript
import { MediaUploader } from '@fluxmedia/core';
import { LocalProvider } from '@fluxmedia/local';

const uploader = new MediaUploader(
  new LocalProvider({
    root: './uploads', // created if missing
    baseUrl: '/media', // where you serve the files
    signingSecret: process.env.MEDIA_SECRET, // 32+ chars, for getSignedUrl()
  })
);

const result = await uploader.upload(buffer, { folder: 'avatars', filename: 'me' });
// result.id === 'avatars/me-x1y2z3a4.png'
```

- Writes are atomic (temp file + rename) and cancellable with `signal`.
- Keys are sanitized and every path is checked to stay inside `root`.
- Metadata is stored in `root/.fluxmedia-meta/`.
- Supports `get`, `delete`, `list`, `copy`, `move`, `download`, `updateMetadata` and `getSignedUrl`.

### Serving files

`createLocalFileHandler` serves files from a Web `Request` handler. It sends `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` and a sandboxing `Content-Security-Policy`, so uploaded HTML or SVG cannot run scripts on your origin.

```typescript
// app/media/[...key]/route.ts
import { createLocalFileHandler } from '@fluxmedia/local';

export const GET = createLocalFileHandler(provider, { pathPrefix: '/media' });
```

With `private: true`, results have no `publicUrl` and the handler only serves valid, unexpired signed URLs from `getSignedUrl()`.

### Configuration

| Option            | Type    | Description                                              |
| ----------------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `root`            | string  | Storage directory (required)                             |
| `baseUrl`         | string  | Base URL used by `getUrl()` (required)                   |
| `private`         | boolean | Omit `publicUrl`; require signatures in the file handler |
| `signingSecret`   | string  | 32+ character secret for signed URLs                     |
| `appendExtension` | boolean | Append the detected extension to keys (default `true`)   |

---

<!-- Source: https://www.fluxmedia.dev/docs/secure-uploads -->

## Secure Uploads and Private Files

How to accept uploads from browsers without opening your bucket to the world, and how to serve files that should not be public.

### The two upload paths

| Path       | How it works                                                  | Use it when                                         |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| **Signed** | Your server signs a short-lived target; the browser uploads straight to storage | Large files, low server load                        |
| **Proxy**  | The browser posts the file to your server, which uploads it   | You need plugins (virus scanning, optimization) to run on every file |

Both are implemented by handlers in `@fluxmedia/core/server`, built on the Web `Request`/`Response` API. They work in Next.js App Router routes, Remix and React Router actions, Hono, SvelteKit, Bun and Deno.

### Signed uploads

```typescript
// app/api/upload/sign/route.ts
import { createSignedUploadHandler } from '@fluxmedia/core/server';
import { uploader } from '@/lib/media';

export const POST = createSignedUploadHandler(uploader, {
  authorize: async (request) => getSessionUser(request), // null → 401
  allowedTypes: ['image/jpeg', 'image/png', 'image/webp'],
  maxSize: 10 * 1024 * 1024,
  folder: (user) => `users/${user.id}`,
  expiresIn: 300,
});
```

The browser sends `{ filename, contentType, size }`. The handler:

1. Answers `401` unless `authorize` returns a user.
2. Answers `413` above `maxSize` and `415` for types outside `allowedTypes`.
3. Builds the key on the server: your `folder`, a sanitized filename and a random suffix. Client-supplied folders and paths are ignored.
4. Returns a `SignedUploadTarget` (`uploadUrl`, `method`, `headers` or `fields`, `storageKey`, `expiresAt`).

What the storage then enforces depends on the provider:

| Provider   | Content type enforced  | Size enforced                     |
| ---------- | ---------------------- | --------------------------------- |
| S3, R2     | Yes (signed header)    | Yes, exact size (signed header)   |
| GCS        | Yes (signed header)    | Yes, upper bound (`x-goog-content-length-range`) |
| Cloudinary | Format (`allowed_formats`) | No — use an upload preset with limits |
| Azure      | No                     | No — check after upload, or use proxy |

On the client:

```tsx
const { upload } = useMediaUpload({ mode: 'signed', signUrlEndpoint: '/api/upload/sign' });
```

Allow your origin in the bucket's CORS rules (`PUT` for S3/R2/GCS/Azure, `POST` for Cloudinary, with the `Content-Type` header).

### Proxy uploads

```typescript
// app/api/upload/route.ts
import { createProxyUploadHandler } from '@fluxmedia/core/server';

export const POST = createProxyUploadHandler(uploader, {
  authorize: async (request) => getSessionUser(request),
  allowedTypes: ['image/jpeg', 'image/png', 'image/webp', 'application/pdf'],
  maxSize: 25 * 1024 * 1024,
  folder: (user) => `users/${user.id}`,
});
```

The proxy handler requires `Content-Length` and rejects oversized requests before reading the body. It identifies the file from its bytes: a file that claims to be `image/png` but is HTML is rejected. Responses contain only safe fields (no internal metadata), and unexpected errors are answered with a generic `500` (log them with `onError`).

### Allowed types and SVG

`allowedTypes` accepts exact types and wildcards (`image/*`). SVG is never matched by `image/*`: an SVG can contain scripts that run when the file is opened from your domain. List `image/svg+xml` explicitly only if you serve uploads from a separate domain or with a sandboxing Content-Security-Policy.

### Private files

Leave the public URL off and hand out short-lived links:

```typescript
const uploader = new MediaUploader(
  new S3Provider({ region: 'us-east-1', bucket: 'private-docs', publicUrl: false })
);

const result = await uploader.upload(file, { folder: `users/${user.id}` });
result.publicUrl; // undefined

const url = await uploader.getSignedUrl(result, { expiresIn: 300, downloadAs: 'invoice.pdf' });
```

| Provider             | Private by                     | Signed URL                                   |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------- |
| S3                   | `publicUrl: false`             | Presigned GET (max 7 days)                   |
| R2                   | Omitting `publicUrl`           | Presigned GET (max 7 days)                   |
| GCS                  | `publicUrl: false`             | V4 signed URL (max 7 days)                   |
| Azure                | `publicUrl: false`             | SAS (account key or user delegation)         |
| Cloudinary           | `public: false` per upload     | Private download URL, or token auth          |
| Local / R2 bindings  | `private: true` / no `publicUrl` | HMAC URL checked with `verifySignedUrl()`   |

Check ownership before signing. A route that signs any key it is given lets users read each other's files:

```typescript
export async function GET(request: Request) {
  const user = await getSessionUser(request);
  const key = new URL(request.url).searchParams.get('key') ?? '';
  if (!user || !key.startsWith(`users/${user.id}/`)) return new Response('Not found', { status: 404 });
  return Response.json({ url: await uploader.getSignedUrl(key, { expiresIn: 300 }) });
}
```

### Metadata and privacy

Only top-level string, number and boolean metadata values are written to storage. Keys starting with `_` and nested objects stay in your process. This keeps plugin data such as EXIF out of object headers, which can be readable by anyone who can read the object.

The image optimization plugin strips EXIF (including GPS location) by default, and the metadata extraction plugin only extracts GPS with `includeGps: true`.

### Checklist

- Every upload route uses `authorize`, `allowedTypes` and `maxSize`.
- The folder comes from the server (`folder: (user) => …`), never from the request.
- Private buckets use `publicUrl: false` (or no `publicUrl` on R2) and a signing route that checks ownership.
- User uploads are served from a separate domain or with `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` and a sandboxing CSP (`createLocalFileHandler` does this).
- Consider `createVirusScanPlugin` for proxy uploads of documents.

---

<!-- Source: https://www.fluxmedia.dev/docs/plugins -->

## Plugins

Extend FluxMedia with custom functionality using the plugin system.

### Installation

```bash
pnpm add @fluxmedia/plugins

# For image optimization / metadata extraction:
pnpm add sharp
```

### Using Plugins

```typescript
import { MediaUploader } from '@fluxmedia/core';
import { 
  createFileValidationPlugin,
  createAnalyticsPlugin 
} from '@fluxmedia/plugins';

const uploader = new MediaUploader(provider);

// Add plugins
await uploader.use(createFileValidationPlugin({
  maxSize: 10 * 1024 * 1024,
  allowedTypes: ['image/*']
}));

await uploader.use(createAnalyticsPlugin({
  logLevel: 'info'
}));
```

### Available Plugins

#### File Validation

Validates files before upload.

```typescript
import { createFileValidationPlugin } from '@fluxmedia/plugins';

const plugin = createFileValidationPlugin({
  allowedTypes: ['image/*', 'video/mp4'],
  maxSize: 10 * 1024 * 1024, // 10MB
  blockedExtensions: ['.exe', '.bat'],
  useMagicBytes: true,
});
```

#### Image Optimization (Server-side)

Optimizes images using sharp before upload.

```typescript
import { createImageOptimizationPlugin } from '@fluxmedia/plugins';

const plugin = createImageOptimizationPlugin({
  maxWidth: 2000,
  maxHeight: 2000,
  quality: 0.85,
  format: 'webp',
});
```

#### Metadata Extraction

Extracts EXIF data, dimensions, and file hashes. Requires `sharp` as a peer dependency for image metadata.

```typescript
import { createMetadataExtractionPlugin } from '@fluxmedia/plugins';

const plugin = createMetadataExtractionPlugin({
  extractExif: true,        // EXIF data (orientation, camera, GPS)
  extractDimensions: true,  // Image width/height
  hashFile: true,           // Generate file hash
  hashAlgorithm: 'md5',    // 'md5' or 'sha256'
});
```

Extracted metadata is added to `options.metadata.extracted`:

```typescript
interface ExtractedMetadata {
  dimensions?: { width: number; height: number };
  exif?: {
    make?: string;
    model?: string;
    orientation?: number;
    dateTime?: string;
    exposureTime?: number;
    fNumber?: number;
    iso?: number;
    focalLength?: number;
    gps?: { latitude?: number[]; longitude?: number[] };
  };
  hash?: string;
  hashAlgorithm?: string;
}
```

This plugin is marked as `optional: true` — extraction failures won't block uploads.

#### Analytics

Logs and tracks upload operations with **strongly-typed events**. Environment-aware with configurable log levels.

```typescript
import { createAnalyticsPlugin, type TrackFunction } from '@fluxmedia/plugins';

const plugin = createAnalyticsPlugin({
  environment: 'production',  // 'development' | 'production' | 'test' | 'all'
  logLevel: 'info',           // 'none' | 'error' | 'warn' | 'info' | 'debug'
  trackPerformance: true,     // Track upload duration and speed
  console: true,              // Log to console
  // Typed track function — TypeScript verifies event/data match
  track: (event, data) => {
    // event: 'media.upload.started' | 'media.upload.completed' | 'media.delete.completed' | 'media.error'
    myAnalytics.track(event, data);
  },
  // Individual callbacks
  onUploadStart: (file, options) => { /* ... */ },
  onUploadComplete: (result, durationMs) => { /* ... */ },
  onUploadError: (error, file) => { /* ... */ },
  onDelete: (id) => { /* ... */ },
});
```

**Event Types:** `media.upload.started`, `media.upload.completed`, `media.delete.completed`, `media.error`

Performance metadata is automatically added to upload results when `trackPerformance: true`:

```typescript
result.metadata.performance = {
  duration: 1234,       // ms
  uploadSpeed: 524288,  // bytes/sec
};
```

This plugin is marked as `optional: true` — analytics failures won't block uploads.

#### Retry

Retries failed uploads with exponential backoff and jitter. The plugin wraps the provider upload (`wrapUpload` hook), so registering it is enough.

```typescript
import { createRetryPlugin, withRetry } from '@fluxmedia/plugins';
import { MediaErrorCode } from '@fluxmedia/core';

await uploader.use(
  createRetryPlugin({
    maxRetries: 3,
    retryDelay: 1000,
    maxDelay: 30_000,
    retryableErrors: [
      MediaErrorCode.NETWORK_ERROR,
      MediaErrorCode.RATE_LIMITED,
      MediaErrorCode.PROVIDER_ERROR,
      MediaErrorCode.UPLOAD_FAILED,
    ],
    onRetry: (attempt, error, delay) => {
      console.log(`Retry ${attempt} after ${delay}ms`);
    },
  })
);

await uploader.upload(file); // retried automatically

// withRetry wraps any async function
const info = await withRetry(() => uploader.get(id), { maxRetries: 2 });
```

**Key features:**
- Exponential backoff with jitter (delays roughly double each retry, capped by `maxDelay`)
- Streams are never retried (they can only be read once)
- Aborted uploads are never retried, and waiting stops as soon as the upload's `signal` aborts
- Custom `shouldRetry` function for fine-grained control


---

#### Virus Scanning

```typescript
import { createVirusScanPlugin, createClamAVScanner } from '@fluxmedia/plugins';

await uploader.use(createVirusScanPlugin({ scan: createClamAVScanner({ host: 'clamav' }) }));
```

Rejects infected files. Fails closed when the scanner is unreachable (`onScannerError: 'allow'` to change), and rejects streams by default (`streams: 'skip'` to change). `scan` can be any `(buffer, info) => Promise<{ clean, threat? }>`.

#### Deduplication

```typescript
import { createDeduplicationPlugin } from '@fluxmedia/plugins';

await uploader.use(createDeduplicationPlugin({ store: myStore }));
```

Returns the existing result for content already uploaded to the same folder (`metadata.deduplicated: true`). Scoped per folder by default so one user's file is never returned for another user.

#### Placeholders

```typescript
import { createPlaceholderPlugin } from '@fluxmedia/plugins';

await uploader.use(createPlaceholderPlugin({ size: 16 }));
// result.metadata.placeholder → { dataUri, dominantColor, width, height }
```

---

### Creating Custom Plugins

#### Using createPlugin Helper

```typescript
import { createPlugin } from '@fluxmedia/core';

const myPlugin = createPlugin('my-plugin', {
  beforeUpload: async (file, options) => {
    console.log('Uploading:', file);
    return { file, options };
  },
  afterUpload: async (result) => {
    console.log('Uploaded:', result.url);
    return result;
  },
  onError: async (error, context) => {
    console.error(`Failed in ${context.phase} phase:`, error.message);
  },
}, { optional: true }); // Optional plugins degrade gracefully
```

#### Manual Plugin Definition

```typescript
import type { FluxMediaPlugin } from '@fluxmedia/core';

const watermarkPlugin: FluxMediaPlugin = {
  name: 'watermark',
  version: '1.0.0',
  optional: false,  // Errors will propagate (default behavior)
  
  async init() {
    // Called when registered via uploader.use()
    console.log('Watermark plugin initialized');
  },
  
  async destroy() {
    // Called when unregistered via uploader.plugins.unregister()
    console.log('Watermark plugin destroyed');
  },
  
  hooks: {
    beforeUpload: async (file, options) => {
      // Add watermark to image...
      return { file: watermarkedFile, options };
    },
  },
};
```

---

### Plugin Lifecycle

#### Registration & Initialization

When a plugin is registered with `uploader.use()`:

1. If a plugin with the same name exists, it is unregistered first (calling `destroy()`)
2. The new plugin's `init()` method is called (if defined)
3. The plugin is stored in the plugin manager

#### Optional Plugins

Plugins with `optional: true` enable graceful degradation:

```typescript
const plugin = createPlugin('non-critical', {
  afterUpload: async (result) => {
    await sendToAnalytics(result); // If this throws...
    return result;
  },
}, { optional: true }); // ...the upload still succeeds
```

When an optional plugin's hook throws:
- The error is caught silently
- The upload pipeline continues
- Useful for analytics, logging, metadata extraction

#### Plugin Hooks

Hooks execute in registration order:

- **beforeUpload** - Modify file/options before upload. Return `{ file, options }` to modify, or `void` to pass through.
- **afterUpload** - Modify result after upload. Must return `UploadResult`.
- **onError** - Handle upload errors. Receives `phase` (`'before'`, `'upload'`, or `'after'`) and optional `uploadResult`.
- **beforeDelete** - Modify ID before deletion. Return new ID or `void`.
- **afterDelete** - Run code after deletion.
- **beforeGetUrl** - Modify URL generation parameters.

---

### Plugin Manager API

```typescript
// Check if plugin exists
uploader.plugins.has('logger');

// Get a plugin
const plugin = uploader.plugins.get('logger');

// Unregister (calls destroy())
await uploader.plugins.unregister('logger');

// Get all plugins
const allPlugins = uploader.plugins.getAll();

// Clear all (calls destroy() on each)
await uploader.plugins.clear();
```

### Plugin Override Behavior

When registering plugins with the same name, the last one wins:

```typescript
// First version
await uploader.use(createPlugin('analytics', {
  afterUpload: async (result) => {
    sendToAnalytics('v1', result);
    return result;
  },
}));

// Override with new version — previous version's destroy() is called
await uploader.use(createPlugin('analytics', {
  afterUpload: async (result) => {
    sendToAnalytics('v2', result); // This one runs
    return result;
  },
}));
```

---

<!-- Source: https://www.fluxmedia.dev/docs/react -->

## React Integration

Hooks and components for React applications.

### Installation

```bash
pnpm add @fluxmedia/core @fluxmedia/react
```

### useMediaUpload Hook

The primary hook for handling uploads in React:

```tsx
import { useMediaUpload } from '@fluxmedia/react';

function UploadForm() {
  const { upload, uploading, progress, result, error, reset } = useMediaUpload({
    mode: 'signed',
    signUrlEndpoint: '/api/upload/sign',
    onUploadComplete: (result) => console.log('Done:', result.url),
    onUploadError: (error) => console.error('Failed:', error),
  });

  return (
    <div>
      <input
        type="file"
        accept="image/*"
        disabled={uploading}
        onChange={(e) => {
          const file = e.target.files?.[0];
          if (file) upload(file, { folder: 'uploads' });
        }}
      />
      
      {uploading && <progress value={progress} max={100} />}
      {result && <img src={result.url} alt="Uploaded" />}
      {error && <p>Error: {error.message}</p>}
      
      <button onClick={reset}>Reset</button>
    </div>
  );
}
```

#### Hook Options

```typescript
interface UseMediaUploadConfig {
  mode: 'signed' | 'proxy';  // 'direct' is rejected: it would expose credentials
  signUrlEndpoint?: string;  // For 'signed' mode (createSignedUploadHandler)
  proxyEndpoint?: string;    // For 'proxy' mode (createProxyUploadHandler)
  headers?: Record<string, string> | (() => Record<string, string> | Promise<Record<string, string>>);
  credentials?: RequestCredentials; // default 'same-origin'
  accept?: string | string[]; // client-side check: 'image/*', 'application/pdf', '.png'
  maxSize?: number;           // client-side check, in bytes
  defaultOptions?: {
    folder?: string;
    tags?: string[];
  };
  onUploadStart?: () => void;
  onUploadComplete?: (result: UploadResult) => void;
  onUploadError?: (error: Error) => void;
}
```

Client-side checks only give quick feedback; the server handlers enforce the real limits.

#### Hook Return Values

```typescript
interface UseMediaUploadReturn {
  upload: (file: File, options?: ClientUploadOptions) => Promise<UploadResult>;
  cancel: () => void;        // abort the upload in progress
  uploading: boolean;
  progress: number; // 0-100
  result: UploadResult | null;
  error: Error | null;       // UploadClientError with kind and status
  reset: () => void;

  // Preview functionality
  preview: string | null;          // Object URL for preview
  setPreview: (file: File | null) => void;  // Set preview from file

  // File type detection (magic bytes, first 4 KB only)
  fileType: { mime: string; ext: string } | null;
  detectFileType: (file: File) => Promise<{ mime: string; ext: string } | null>;
}
```

For many files, `useMediaUploadQueue(config, { concurrency })` tracks status, progress and errors per file, with `cancel(id)` and `retry(id)`. `<MediaUpload>` exposes `getRootProps()` and `isDragging` for drag-and-drop.


### Preview Before Upload

Show a preview of selected files before uploading:

```tsx
function UploadWithPreview() {
  const { upload, preview, setPreview, uploading } = useMediaUpload({
    mode: 'proxy',
    proxyEndpoint: '/api/upload',
  });

  const handleSelect = (e: React.ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement>) => {
    const file = e.target.files?.[0];
    if (file) {
      setPreview(file);  // Creates object URL, handles cleanup
      upload(file);
    }
  };

  return (
    <div>
      {preview && <img src={preview} alt="Preview" />}
      <input type="file" accept="image/*" onChange={handleSelect} />
    </div>
  );
}
```

### File Type Detection

Detect actual file type using magic bytes (more reliable than file extension):

```tsx
function ValidatedUpload() {
  const { upload, detectFileType, fileType } = useMediaUpload({
    mode: 'proxy',
    proxyEndpoint: '/api/upload',
  });

  const handleSelect = async (e: React.ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement>) => {
    const file = e.target.files?.[0];
    if (!file) return;

    const type = await detectFileType(file);
    
    if (!type?.mime.startsWith('image/')) {
      alert('Please select an image file');
      return;
    }

    await upload(file);
  };

  return (
    <div>
      <input type="file" onChange={handleSelect} />
      {fileType && <p>Detected: {fileType.mime}</p>}
    </div>
  );
}
```

### Provider Selection

Pass provider selection to upload:

```tsx
function MultiProviderUpload() {
  const [provider, setProvider] = useState<'cloudinary' | 's3' | 'r2'>('cloudinary');
  const { upload } = useMediaUpload({
    mode: 'proxy',
    proxyEndpoint: '/api/upload',
  });

  const handleUpload = (file: File) => {
    upload(file, {
      folder: 'uploads',
      provider,  // Passed to server endpoint
      metadata: { description: 'User upload' },  // Custom metadata
    });
  };

  return (
    <div>
      <select value={provider} onChange={(e) => setProvider(e.target.value as any)}>
        <option value="cloudinary">Cloudinary</option>
        <option value="s3">AWS S3</option>
        <option value="r2">Cloudflare R2</option>
      </select>
      <input type="file" onChange={(e) => handleUpload(e.target.files![0])} />
    </div>
  );
}
```

### Upload Modes

#### Signed Upload (Recommended)

Browser gets a signed URL from your server, then uploads directly to the provider.

```tsx
const { upload } = useMediaUpload({
  mode: 'signed',
  signUrlEndpoint: '/api/upload/sign',
});
```

**Server endpoint (Next.js):**

```typescript
// app/api/upload/sign/route.ts
import crypto from 'crypto';

export async function POST(request: Request) {
  const { filename, folder } = await request.json();
  
  const timestamp = Math.round(Date.now() / 1000);
  const signature = crypto
    .createHash('sha1')
    .update(`folder=${folder}&timestamp=${timestamp}${apiSecret}`)
    .digest('hex');

  return Response.json({
    uploadUrl: `https://api.cloudinary.com/v1_1/${cloudName}/auto/upload`,
    fields: { api_key, timestamp, signature, folder },
  });
}
```

#### Proxy Upload

Upload goes through your server (more control, slightly slower).

```tsx
const { upload } = useMediaUpload({
  mode: 'proxy',
  proxyEndpoint: '/api/upload',
});
```

**Server endpoint:**

```typescript
// app/api/upload/route.ts
import { MediaUploader } from '@fluxmedia/core';
import { CloudinaryProvider } from '@fluxmedia/cloudinary';

export async function POST(request: Request) {
  const formData = await request.formData();
  const file = formData.get('file') as File;
  
  const uploader = new MediaUploader(new CloudinaryProvider({ ... }));
  const buffer = Buffer.from(await file.arrayBuffer());
  const result = await uploader.upload(buffer);
  
  return Response.json(result);
}
```

### MediaUpload Component

A render-prop component for more complex UIs:

```tsx
import { MediaUpload } from '@fluxmedia/react';

function FileUploader() {
  return (
    <MediaUpload
      config={{ mode: 'signed', signUrlEndpoint: '/api/upload/sign' }}
      accept="image/*"
      maxSize={5 * 1024 * 1024}
      onComplete={(results) => console.log('Uploaded:', results)}
      onError={(error) => console.error(error)}
    >
      {({ uploading, progress, result, error, openFileDialog }) => (
        <div>
          <button onClick={openFileDialog} disabled={uploading}>
            {uploading ? `Uploading ${progress}%` : 'Select File'}
          </button>
          {result && <img src={result.url} alt="Uploaded" />}
        </div>
      )}
    </MediaUpload>
  );
}
```

#### Component Props

| Prop | Type | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| `config` | UseMediaUploadConfig | Upload configuration |
| `accept` | string | Accepted file types |
| `multiple` | boolean | Allow multiple files |
| `maxSize` | number | Max file size in bytes |
| `onSelect` | (files: File[]) => void | Called when files selected |
| `onComplete` | (results: UploadResult[]) => void | Called after upload |
| `onError` | (error: Error) => void | Called on error |

<!-- Source: https://www.fluxmedia.dev/docs/api -->

## API Reference

Complete API documentation for FluxMedia packages.

### MediaUploader

The main class for uploading files. Supports fallback providers, transactional uploads, and plugin orchestration.

#### Constructor

```typescript
new MediaUploader(
  provider: MediaProvider,
  plugins?: FluxMediaPlugin[],
  config?: MediaUploaderConfig
)
```

**Parameters:**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `provider` | `MediaProvider` | Primary storage provider |
| `plugins` | `FluxMediaPlugin[]` | Optional array of plugins to register |
| `config` | `MediaUploaderConfig` | Optional configuration for fallback, error handling |

#### MediaUploaderConfig

```typescript
interface MediaUploaderConfig {
  fallbackProvider?: MediaProvider;
  fallbackOnErrors?: MediaErrorCode[];
  onFallback?: (error: MediaError, fallbackProvider: MediaProvider) => void;
}
```

| Option | Type | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| `fallbackProvider` | `MediaProvider` | Provider to use when primary fails |
| `fallbackOnErrors` | `MediaErrorCode[]` | Error codes that trigger fallback (default: network, rate-limit, provider errors) |
| `onFallback` | `function` | Callback when fallback is triggered |

**Example:**

```typescript
import { MediaUploader, MediaErrorCode } from '@fluxmedia/core';

const uploader = new MediaUploader(
  primaryProvider,
  [analyticsPlugin],
  {
    fallbackProvider: backupProvider,
    fallbackOnErrors: [
      MediaErrorCode.NETWORK_ERROR,
      MediaErrorCode.RATE_LIMITED,
      MediaErrorCode.PROVIDER_ERROR,
    ],
    onFallback: (error, provider) => {
      console.warn(`Falling back to ${provider.name}: ${error.message}`);
    },
  }
);
```

#### Methods

##### upload(file, options?)

Upload a single file. Runs `beforeUpload` hooks, the provider upload (wrapped by `wrapUpload` hooks such as retry), then `afterUpload` hooks. Fails over to the fallback provider on qualifying errors (never for streams).

```typescript
async upload(file: UploadInput, options?: UploadOptions): Promise<UploadResult>
```

##### File references

Every method below that takes a `ref` accepts a file ID / storage key or the `UploadResult` returned by `upload()`. Passing the result routes the call to the provider that stored the file (after a failover) and passes hints such as Cloudinary's resource type.

```typescript
type FileRef = string | UploadResult;
```

##### delete(ref) / deleteMultiple(refs)

```typescript
async delete(ref: FileRef): Promise<void>
async deleteMultiple(refs: FileRef[], options?: { concurrency?: number }): Promise<void>
```

Plain IDs are deleted with the provider's batch API (S3/R2 `DeleteObjects`). Throws `DELETE_FAILED` with `details.failedIds` when some deletes fail. Deleting a missing file succeeds.

##### get(ref) / exists(ref)

```typescript
async get(ref: FileRef): Promise<UploadResult>     // FILE_NOT_FOUND if missing
async exists(ref: FileRef): Promise<boolean>
```

##### getUrl(ref, transform?) / getUrlAsync(ref, transform?)

`getUrl` is synchronous; `getUrlAsync` also runs `beforeGetUrl` hooks. For private storage the URL is not readable — use `getSignedUrl`.

```typescript
getUrl(ref: FileRef, transform?: TransformationOptions): string
async getUrlAsync(ref: FileRef, transform?: TransformationOptions): Promise<string>
```

##### getSignedUrl(ref, options?)

Time-limited URL for reading a private file.

```typescript
async getSignedUrl(ref: FileRef, options?: {
  expiresIn?: number;        // seconds, default 3600 (S3/R2/GCS/Azure max 7 days)
  downloadAs?: string;       // force a download with this filename
  transform?: TransformationOptions; // Cloudinary with token auth
}): Promise<string>
```

##### createUploadUrl(options)

Signed target for a direct browser upload. Expose it through `createSignedUploadHandler` (see Secure Uploads) rather than directly.

```typescript
async createUploadUrl(options: {
  contentType: string;       // signed on S3, R2 and GCS
  size?: number;             // exact size on S3/R2, upper bound on GCS
  filename?: string;
  folder?: string;
  expiresIn?: number;        // default 600
  uniqueFilename?: boolean;
  metadata?: Record<string, unknown>;
  tags?: string[];
  cacheControl?: string;
  contentDisposition?: string;
  public?: boolean;
}): Promise<SignedUploadTarget>

interface SignedUploadTarget {
  uploadUrl: string;
  method: 'PUT' | 'POST';
  headers?: Record<string, string>; // send with PUT
  fields?: Record<string, string>;  // send before "file" with POST
  storageKey: string;
  publicUrl?: string;
  expiresAt: Date;
  provider: string;
}
```

##### list(options?) / listAll(options?)

```typescript
async list(options?: { folder?: string; limit?: number; cursor?: string }): Promise<{
  items: UploadResult[];
  nextCursor?: string;
}>

for await (const file of uploader.listAll({ folder: 'invoices' })) {
  // follows cursors for you
}
```

##### search(query)

Supported by Cloudinary (Search API). Other providers throw `NOT_SUPPORTED`; use `list`.

##### copy(ref, toId) / move(ref, toId)

```typescript
async copy(ref: FileRef, toId: string): Promise<UploadResult>
async move(ref: FileRef, toId: string): Promise<UploadResult>
```

##### download(ref)

```typescript
async download(ref: FileRef): Promise<{
  body: ReadableStream<Uint8Array>;
  contentType?: string;
  size?: number;
}>
```

##### updateMetadata(ref, metadata)

Replaces the file's custom metadata (top-level primitive values only).

```typescript
async updateMetadata(ref: FileRef, metadata: Record<string, unknown>): Promise<void>
```

##### uploadMultiple(files, options?)

Uploads with a concurrency limit, running plugins for each file. When any upload fails it throws a `MediaError` whose `details.succeeded` holds the results that did upload and `details.failed` the errors by index.

```typescript
async uploadMultiple(
  files: UploadInput[],
  options?: UploadOptions & { concurrency?: number } // default 3
): Promise<UploadResult[]>
```

##### uploadWithTransaction(file, options, callbacks)

Upload, then commit; if the commit throws, the upload is rolled back (`onRollback`, or deleted from the provider that stored it).

```typescript
async uploadWithTransaction<T>(
  file: UploadInput,
  options: UploadOptions,
  callbacks: TransactionCallbacks<T>
): Promise<{ uploadResult: UploadResult; commitResult: T }>

interface TransactionCallbacks<T> {
  onCommit: (result: UploadResult) => Promise<T>;
  onRollback?: (result: UploadResult, error: Error) => Promise<void>;
}
```

**Example:**

```typescript
const { uploadResult, commitResult } = await uploader.uploadWithTransaction(
  file,
  { folder: 'documents' },
  {
    onCommit: async (result) => {
      return await db.documents.create({ storageKey: result.storageKey, provider: result.provider });
    },
  }
);
```

##### ready()

Resolves once constructor plugins are initialized; rejects if one's `init()` failed.

##### supports(feature)

Check if provider supports a feature.

```typescript
supports(feature: string): boolean
```

##### use(plugin)

Register a plugin. Calls `plugin.init()` if defined.

```typescript
async use(plugin: FluxMediaPlugin): Promise<this>
```

---

### Types

#### UploadInput

Union type for all accepted upload inputs:

```typescript
type UploadInput = File | Buffer | Readable | ReadableStream;
```

Supports browser `File` objects, Node.js `Buffer`, Node.js `Readable` streams, and web `ReadableStream`.

#### UploadOptions

```typescript
interface UploadOptions {
  folder?: string;
  filename?: string;
  public?: boolean;
  tags?: string[];
  metadata?: Record<string, unknown>;
  transformation?: TransformationOptions;
  onProgress?: (percent: number) => void;
  onByteProgress?: (loaded: number, total: number | undefined) => void;
  uniqueFilename?: boolean;     // Append a random suffix (default: true)
  contentType?: string;         // Required for streams
  cacheControl?: string;
  contentDisposition?: string;
  signal?: AbortSignal;
  providerOptions?: Record<string, unknown>;
}
```

| Option | Type | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| `folder` | `string` | Destination folder. Sanitized: `..` segments and unsafe characters are removed |
| `filename` | `string` | Custom filename (without extension), sanitized the same way |
| `public` | `boolean` | Visibility. Cloudinary stores `false` as `authenticated`; S3 applies an ACL with `useAcl`; requests a bucket cannot honour fail |
| `tags` | `string[]` | Tags (S3/R2 object tags, Cloudinary tags) |
| `metadata` | `Record<string, unknown>` | Custom metadata. Only top-level string/number/boolean values are stored; `_`-prefixed keys and nested objects stay in-process |
| `transformation` | `TransformationOptions` | Apply transformations on upload (Cloudinary) |
| `onProgress` | `(percent: number) => void` | Normalized 0-100 progress callback |
| `onByteProgress` | `(loaded, total) => void` | Byte progress; `total` is undefined for streams |
| `uniqueFilename` | `boolean` | Append a random suffix (default: `true`) |
| `contentType` | `string` | MIME type; required for streams (Buffers and Files are detected from content) |
| `cacheControl` | `string` | `Cache-Control` for the stored object |
| `contentDisposition` | `string` | `Content-Disposition` for the stored object |
| `signal` | `AbortSignal` | Cancel the upload (`ABORTED` error) |
| `providerOptions` | `Record<string, unknown>` | Native parameters, e.g. S3 `StorageClass`. Never from client input |

#### UploadResult

```typescript
interface UploadResult {
  id: string;
  storageKey: string;
  url: string;
  publicUrl?: string;
  size: number;
  format: string;
  width?: number;
  height?: number;
  provider: string;
  metadata: Record<string, unknown>;
  createdAt: Date;
}
```

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `id` | `string` | Unique identifier for the uploaded file |
| `storageKey` | `string` | Provider-specific storage key (e.g., S3 object key, Cloudinary public ID) |
| `url` | `string` | Direct URL to the file |
| `publicUrl` | `string` (optional) | Public URL. Omitted for private storage served through signed URLs |
| `size` | `number` | File size in bytes |
| `format` | `string` | File format/extension |
| `width` | `number` | Image width (if applicable) |
| `height` | `number` | Image height (if applicable) |
| `provider` | `string` | Provider name that handled the upload |
| `metadata` | `Record<string, unknown>` | Additional metadata |
| `createdAt` | `Date` | Upload timestamp |

#### TransformationOptions

```typescript
interface TransformationOptions {
  width?: number;
  height?: number;
  fit?: 'cover' | 'contain' | 'fill' | 'inside' | 'outside';
  quality?: number;
  format?: 'auto' | 'webp' | 'avif' | 'jpg' | 'png';
}
```

#### MediaProvider

```typescript
interface MediaProvider {
  readonly name: string;
  readonly features: ProviderFeatures;
  readonly native: unknown;

  upload(file: UploadInput, options?: UploadOptions): Promise<UploadResult>;
  delete(id: string, options?: ResourceOptions): Promise<void>;
  get(id: string, options?: ResourceOptions): Promise<UploadResult>;
  getUrl(id: string, transform?: TransformationOptions, options?: ResourceOptions): string;
  uploadMultiple(files: UploadInput[], options?: UploadOptions): Promise<UploadResult[]>;
  deleteMultiple(ids: string[], options?: ResourceOptions): Promise<void>;

  // Optional capabilities
  getSignedUrl?(id: string, options?: SignedUrlOptions): Promise<string>;
  createUploadUrl?(options: SignedUploadOptions): Promise<SignedUploadTarget>;
  exists?(id: string, options?: ResourceOptions): Promise<boolean>;
  list?(options?: ListOptions): Promise<ListResult>;
  search?(query: SearchOptions): Promise<UploadResult[]>;
  copy?(fromId: string, toId: string, options?: ResourceOptions): Promise<UploadResult>;
  move?(fromId: string, toId: string, options?: ResourceOptions): Promise<UploadResult>;
  download?(id: string, options?: ResourceOptions): Promise<DownloadResult>;
  updateMetadata?(id: string, metadata: Record<string, unknown>, options?: ResourceOptions): Promise<void>;
}

// Hints from an UploadResult's metadata (e.g. Cloudinary resourceType)
interface ResourceOptions {
  metadata?: Record<string, unknown>;
}
```

#### ProviderFeatures

```typescript
interface ProviderFeatures {
  transformations: {
    resize: boolean;
    crop: boolean;
    format: boolean;
    quality: boolean;
    blur: boolean;
    rotate: boolean;
    effects: boolean;
  };
  capabilities: {
    signedUploads: boolean;
    directUpload: boolean;
    multipartUpload: boolean;
    videoProcessing: boolean;
    aiTagging: boolean;
    facialDetection: boolean;
    signedUrls?: boolean;
    list?: boolean;
    search?: boolean;
    copy?: boolean;
    download?: boolean;
    updateMetadata?: boolean;
  };
  storage: {
    maxFileSize: number;
    supportedFormats: string[];
  };
}
```

### File Type Detection

Detect file types using magic bytes (more reliable than extensions).

#### getFileType(buffer)

```typescript
import { getFileType } from '@fluxmedia/core';

const type = await getFileType(buffer);
console.log(type); // { mime: 'image/jpeg', ext: 'jpg' }
```

#### getFileTypeFromStream(stream)

For large files without loading into memory:

```typescript
import { getFileTypeFromStream } from '@fluxmedia/core';

const type = await getFileTypeFromStream(readableStream);
```

#### Helper Functions

```typescript
import { isImage, isVideo } from '@fluxmedia/core';

if (await isImage(buffer)) {
  // Handle image
}

if (await isVideo(buffer)) {
  // Handle video
}
```
